title: Some petal diagrams of the unknot are hard
summary: A petal diagram of a knot is a projection with a single multi-crossing and no nested loops; it is encoded by a permutation of the heights of the strands through the multi-crossing. Colton, Glover, Hughes and Sandberg proved a Reidemeister-type theorem for petal diagrams: two petal permutations represent the same knot if and only if they are related by trivial petal additions and deletions and by crossing exchanges.
